questions.question: What is the main purpose of a disease-modifying antirheumatic drug in inflammatory disease?
choices: Reduce disease activity and help prevent or limit inflammatory damage
Provide immediate analgesia only
Replace assessment for infection
Eliminate all need for rheumatology follow-up
questions.explanation: DMARDs are used to modify the inflammatory disease process. Symptom relief alone may not control disease activity or prevent damage.

questions.question: What is the safest first step before advising a patient on a biologic or targeted therapy?
choices: Verify the exact drug, route, schedule, last dose, indication, prescriber, and monitoring plan
Assume every injection has the same risk
Give blanket instructions to stop the medication
Base the decision only on the diagnosis name
questions.explanation: Safety decisions are medication- and patient-specific. The exact therapy and established plan determine appropriate screening, monitoring, and action.

questions.question: A patient receiving immune-modulating therapy reports fever, cough, and worsening fatigue. What is the best FNP approach?
choices: Assess severity and possible infection, then contact the prescribing team for medication-specific guidance
Tell the patient to take the next dose without assessment
Assume the symptoms are a routine flare
Ignore symptoms unless a high fever is documented
questions.explanation: Immune-modulating therapies can increase infection risk and alter presentation. Evaluate the patient and use the specialty plan rather than giving reflex medication advice.

questions.question: Why should repeated systemic corticosteroid bursts prompt reassessment?
choices: They can create cumulative adverse effects and may indicate uncontrolled disease or an incomplete treatment plan
They have no meaningful long-term risks
They permanently cure inflammatory disease
They eliminate the need for monitoring glucose or blood pressure
questions.explanation: Repeated systemic corticosteroid exposure can affect glucose, blood pressure, bone health, infection risk, mood, sleep, and other systems. It may also signal a need for better disease control.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects safe JAK-inhibitor risk thinking?
choices: Review the product-specific plan and cardiovascular, thrombotic, infection, malignancy, and patient-specific risks
Assume all oral therapies are low risk
Use a refill request as the only assessment needed
Ignore new chest pain or unilateral leg swelling
questions.explanation: Certain JAK inhibitors have prominent safety warnings. New cardiopulmonary or thrombotic symptoms require urgent assessment rather than a routine refill discussion.

questions.question: A patient on an immunomodulator has a hot swollen joint, fever, and rapidly worsening pain. What should be prioritized?
choices: Urgent evaluation for septic arthritis or another serious process
Routine flare treatment at home without assessment
Waiting for the next scheduled rheumatology visit
Increasing the immunomodulator dose independently
questions.explanation: A hot swollen joint with systemic illness can represent septic arthritis. It requires urgent assessment and should not be presumed to be an inflammatory flare.

questions.question: What is the safest approach to vaccines in a patient receiving a biologic or other immunomodulator?
choices: Use current CDC/ACIP, product-specific, and rheumatology guidance for the exact therapy and timing
Tell every patient that all vaccines are always safe
Tell every patient to avoid all vaccines permanently
Use a schedule remembered from years ago without verification
questions.explanation: Immune suppression can affect vaccine safety and effectiveness. Current guidance and the exact medication plan are required.

questions.question: Before prescribing a new outpatient medication to a patient on DMARDs or biologics, what should the FNP do?
choices: Reconcile the full regimen and check interactions and overlapping toxicities, including supplements and over-the-counter products
Assume a common prescription cannot interact
Stop all rheumatology medicines first
Avoid asking about nonprescription products
questions.explanation: New medicines and supplements can create interaction or organ-toxicity risks. Medication reconciliation is a core safety step.

questions.question: Why is pregnancy planning important in patients receiving rheumatology medications?
choices: Disease activity and some medications have important reproductive implications that need early specialist coordination
It is unrelated to medication safety
All rheumatology medicines have identical pregnancy guidance
A positive pregnancy test means all medicines should be stopped immediately without review
questions.explanation: Medication and disease plans may need adjustment before or during pregnancy. Abrupt changes can also create harm, so early coordinated review is essential.

questions.question: Which handoff information is most useful when contacting rheumatology about a possible therapy complication?
choices: Exact medication and timing, symptom trajectory, severity, vital signs, relevant labs, and the specific question needing guidance
Only the diagnosis name
A request to call back without symptoms
A general statement that the patient feels different
questions.explanation: Focused, structured information allows the prescribing team to assess infection, toxicity, flare, and disposition rapidly.
